scraped.scraped_description:
arXiv is a free distribution service and an open-access archive for nearly 2.4 million
      scholarly articles in the fields of physics, mathematics, computer science, quantitative biology, quantitative finance, statistics, electrical engineering and systems science, and economics.
      Materials on this site are not peer-reviewed by arXiv.

name: arXiv
tagline: Free distribution service and open-access archive for scholarly articles in physics, mathematics, computer science, and related fields
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on institutional support and donations
awards: Recognized as foundational open access infrastructure by UNESCO
Multiple citations in digital scholarship literature
published_performance_metrics: arXiv publishes annual statistics on submissions, downloads, and user engagement
documented_limitations: Materials on site are not peer-reviewed by arXiv
Moderation relies on community standards rather than formal peer review
failure_modes: Occasional moderation delays due to volunteer-dependent system
Spam and low-quality submissions in some subject areas
curation_criteria: Submissions must be original research or significant revisions; moderation based on arXiv policies and community standards; subject-specific advisory boards review policies
contributor_governance: Community-driven moderation with volunteer moderators; advisory boards for different subject areas; Cornell University oversight as host institution
community_ownership: Partial - hosted by Cornell University with community input through advisory boards; not community-owned but community-governed in moderation
controversies: Debates over moderation transparency and appeal processes
Discussions about representation of non-English language research
ai_involvement: arXiv uses machine learning for paper classification and recommendation systems; AI-assisted moderation tools under development
political_relevance_summary: Addresses threats to digital autonomy and privacy rights that affect civic participation and civil liberties.

movement_building_utility.notes: Serves as an information resource for civic actors, researchers, or the public.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (2 countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability. Methodology and approach could inform similar efforts in other jurisdictions.
